verdicts.misleading_risk: Medium. Making inputs/outputs/screenshots required would unlist apps: catalogue.py raises AppProblem on schema failure and the app is left out and named in build/problems.md, so all 6 current apps (none has inputs/outputs; 5 of 6 have 0 screenshots in build/snapshot.json) would vanish. Authors would also be pushed to write filler to get listed, and a 'tested with' or 'example_data' URL would be an unverified claim the site relays. The field set also overlaps the existing free-text 'description' (maxLength 2000) and 'quickstart'.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Add two optional manifest fields, `inputs` and `outputs` (each up to 5 short plain-text strings, e.g. 'CSV or XML tracking tables', 'Track metrics and plots'). Add them to schema/labconstrictor-app.schema.json and to the initialiser's copy in LabConstrictor_streamlit/schemas so authors are asked. Render a 'Works with' / 'Produces' definition list under the lead sentence through optional_list() and esc(), in a small new module so pages_apps.py stays under 300 lines. Append the text to cards.search_text. Do NOT make them required and do NOT add limitations or example_data: authors can say limits in 'description' and link example data from 'quickstart' or docs_url. Instead, in catalogue.py have a missing inputs or outputs for a non-testing app add a warning line to build/problems.md. That surfaces it without delisting, and is not a silent default. Drop the screenshots-required rule: NucleiSky's banner shows that a required screenshot gets filler. Then ask each app author to fill the fields from their own README (CellTracksColab README:152-158 names CSV or XML). Do not write the values on the site side.
verdicts.evidence: Schema has no inputs/outputs/limitations/example_data (read in full). Snapshot manifest keys: only NucleiSky has screenshots (1); none has quickstart. CellTracksColab README:146-158 states the 'Required File Format' (CSV or XML) that the app page lacks. catalogue.py:5 and :81 show that failing validation leaves an app out. DESIGN/AGENTS 'authors expose only what they choose' fits optional fields, not required ones.

verdicts.misleading_risk: Medium. Making quickstart required delists every current app, since none sets it. The generic 'Using it' paragraph is true for installer apps (Welcome notebook plus the guide link), so it is not a hidden fallback; the real gap is that no app gives a first runnable example. The example_data link depends on G1's field, which should be dropped. The template typo claim is partly stale in the right place: 'finnisehd' and 'LabConstrictisct' typos do exist, but the file is src-template/.tools/docs/notebook_usage.md and every app clone carries a copy, so the fix belongs in the template repo only.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Keep 'quickstart' optional. Add a build/problems.md warning, not an error, for any non-testing app without it, so the gap is visible and not silent. In pages_apps.using_section, when a quickstart is present, show it first and keep the generic Welcome-notebook line after it. When absent, keep the generic text (it is true) but say it once in problems.md. Ask the authors of CellTracksColab, NucleiSky and VLab4Mic to write a 3-5 step quickstart in their own manifests (e.g. CellTracksColab: open the loading notebook, load the Zenodo test dataset from README:246, press Run). Separately fix the typos in the template's notebook_usage.md (and src-template) in that repo; no site change.
verdicts.evidence: pages_apps.py:108-120 using_section shows the generic paragraph when m has no quickstart and installer is true; schema quickstart is optional (minItems 1, maxItems 6). No snapshot manifest sets quickstart. grep confirms the typos 'finnisehd' and 'LabConstrisctor' in LabConstrictor/.tools/docs/notebook_usage.md and its copies. catalogue.py unlists schema-invalid apps, so 'required' would remove all 6.

verdicts.misleading_risk: High for the proposal as written. A per-host manifest `status: usable` plus `tested_with: 'napari 0.5.x'` lets authors assert something that the plugins' own docs contradict: napari-labconstrictor, LabConstrictor-Fiji/QuPath/Tools docs/user-guide.md all say 'Under heavy construction ... untested and unlikely to be stable' and 'Tested on Linux'. The site would then show 'usable' against the plugin guide. 'Soon' is currently the one honest site-wide statement and it matches those guides. The real defect is the wording: 'Works in' (filter, pages_apps.py:27) and the Details row 'Works in: napari, Fiji' (pages_apps.py:147) contradict the chip 'Soon in napari', and VLab4Mic's own description says 'Two of its tools also run in Napari and Fiji'.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Keep the manifest `hosts` enum as is. Put the status in one place, data/hosts.yaml, as a `status: soon` field per program (cards.py:63-71 then reads it instead of hard-coding 'Soon'); flip it when the plugin's own guide drops the 'under heavy construction' banner. Rename the filter label to 'Also in (soon)' and the Details row to 'Tools in (soon)' or 'Planned in' so the two agree, and make /guides/napari/ and the chip say the same. Update DESIGN.md:49 first (AGENTS.md rule). Ask the VLab4Mic author to reword 'also run in Napari and Fiji' to say which tools and that the plugins are experimental (GuessTheCondition README:55-67 already lists its five tools, so a tool list is something authors can already write in their description). Skip per-app status, tools and tested_with fields.
verdicts.evidence: cards.py:63-71 hard-codes 'Soon in'. pages_apps.py:27 select("host", "Works in"), :147 rows.append(("Works in", ...)). Snapshot: VLab4Mic hosts [notebook, napari, fiji]; Guess the Condition adds napari, fiji; Playground adds qupath. /home/user/napari-labconstrictor/docs/user-guide.md:6-8 and LabConstrictor-Tools/docs/user-guide.md:8 carry the 'untested' banner. data/hosts.yaml has name/url/plugin/logo and no status.

verdicts.misleading_risk: Low. No claim on the page changes; it is a markup and behaviour fix. Risks are regressions: check_site.py menu_problems and check_design.py find 'ul.lc-menu' and the active class but not DOM order, so they should still pass; test_site.py:258 builds fake pages and does not assert order.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Reproduced: at 390 px, Tab goes Skip, LabConstrictor, Menu (35x35 checkbox); Space opens the drawer; the next Tab lands on the page content (the Search input) not on the menu links, because <ul class="lc-menu"> sits before .lc-header__tools in overrides/main.html:32-43. The search button is 0x0 on phone. Smallest fix: move the burger checkbox in the markup before the <ul> (brand, burger, ul, search), so a Tab after opening reaches 'Home'; on desktop the burger is display:none so it stays out of tab order and visual order is unchanged with flex `order` on the burger/search wrapper. Add aria-expanded to the checkbox in lc.js (set on change) and extend lcInitMenu's Escape so it listens on the nav (keydown Escape on any link closes the drawer and focuses the checkbox). Add one test to check_design.py or a small Playwright check at 390 px: after opening, Tab reaches the first menu link. Keep each function under 30 lines.
verdicts.evidence: My Playwright run (node, chromium-1194, 390x800, /apps/): focus sequence ['A Skip to content', 'A LabConstrictor', 'INPUT Menu 35x35', 'SPACE', 'INPUT  309x45' (the filter search), 'SELECT ...']; menu links are ['Home','Apps','Docs','Ecosystem','Submit your app']; .md-search__button width 0. overrides/main.html:32-43 order confirmed; lc.js:95-101 Escape handler is on the checkbox only; lc.css:55-77 shows the drawer shown via :has(.lc-menu-toggle:checked).
